## CELL FACTS

Cell 土_劫财 (Earth carrying The Rival). Persona The Rival (劫财). Definition line: "Same nature, different register, the edge of comparison". Keyword Rivalry, charge fierce, poles catalyst Daring / friction Drain. Family function: Body. Cost dimension: comparison as fuel; the race never announces a finish. Arena: the race, the shared prize, the other runner. Classical portrait: same nature, different register; comparison as fuel; the race with no announced finish. Ruled domains: Rivalry, Shared stakes, Boldness. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 比肩.
Element arena: Earth (ground, soil, load, field, bedrock, harvest). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Earth. structural_interaction seed: "Stability meeting stability cross-polarity — ground competing with ground".
- k2_overview: "Your Earth moves as the Rival: ground that expands by wager. You bet acreage where others bet coins, patient about the campaign, bold about the claim. Shared land, family stakes, and joint holdings follow you through life. You win them by daring and keep them by the paperwork you almost skipped."
- k2_functional: "Your energy is heavy machinery: slow to start, formidable engaged, needing scheduled idle."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Territorial","Holds grudges","Bulldozing"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Rivalry":"Your rivalries are territorial and patient: the competing shop, the sibling’s acreage, the slow contest of estates. Compete by building better rather than holding harder. Ground won by improvement stays won.","Shared stakes":"Everything significant you own will at some point be co-owned: family land, joint ventures, marriages of assets. Survey early, deed clearly, and revisit the map annually. Your fortune lives in shared soil.","Boldness":"Your daring moves mountains occasionally: the land bought unseen, the advantage taken calmly. Because your bets are heavy, space them. Earth recovers slowly from the ones that slide."}

- Sibling cell 土_比肩 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Your footing comes from inside your own boundaries, and it shows in how little you sway. Trends pass, opinions swirl, someone is always panicking about something, and your center of gravity stays home. People push against you mostly to find out where solid feels like."

Core element Earth, energy element Earth. Law: Earth and Earth are the same element (the self pair). Relative to the core the energy is the self, so Earth is this core's Body. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Earth core that shows Earth on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Earth as the Body is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 土_土's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: You are better with a rival in sight. Your own pace never quite wakes you, so you measure yourself against a person rather than a plan. Pick your rivals on purpose, and you turn a reflex into the fastest way you grow.

value_b.text: Competition wakes something in you that nothing else reaches. Being measured against someone feels more honest than being measured alone, and you push harder for a rival than for a fan. Keep one rival close, and you keep your best effort within reach.

value.text: Being better with rivals leaves you rarely at your best alone. Without someone to beat, you drift rather than push, so the goals only you care about wait longest. Find a rival for the private goals too, and you stop leaving your own for last.

value.text: You bet big because only a real stake gets all of you, and you would rather risk a lot on one move than a little on many. If you let small bets count too, you stop missing the gains that come slowly.

value_b.text: Betting big, you find out what you are made of. You value one bold bet more than many safe ones, and you will stake a season on it. Leave a quiet stretch after each big bet to come back to the next one whole.

value.text: On a shared stake, you bet someone else's year with your own. You would rather win it all for both of you than keep half safe, and their caution becomes your dare. Ask first, because you keep a partner who chose the risk.

value.text: With a win in hand, you would rather share the credit than keep it, because a prize means more with your people inside it. When a win can count before you have shared it, you get to enjoy it twice.

value_b.text: Whenever you come out ahead, you share the credit first. You want to be seen winning as much as you want the prize. Once you enjoy a result nobody saw, you share the credit freely instead of trading it for an audience.

value.text: Taking the credit alone feels like showing off to you. You hand out credit rather than keep it, and your own work goes unnamed. If you put your own name on your part, you stop losing the chances that follow credit.

value.text: The credit you share lands on people who did not run for it. You would rather have company at the finish than stand there alone, and you pass out what only you earned. Name who did what, to give praise each person can use.
